newsitem.title: JAMAICA: CRICKET-W.INDIES TAKE FIRST INNINGS LEAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-W.INDIES TAKE FIRST INNINGS LEAD.

text.p: West Indies took a first innings lead of 81 runs as they bowled out India for 346 on the fourth day of the first cricket test at Sabina Park on Sunday.
In eight overs before lunch the West Indies had reached 29 without loss in their second innings with Sherwin Campbell on 17 and the recalled Stuart Williams on 12.
The pair took 20 runs off the first two overs by pacemen Abey Kuruvilla and Venkatesh Prasad, forcing India to set a less adventurous field.

Debutant paceman Franklyn Rose, scourge of the Indian batsmen on Saturday when he took five wickets, added Kuruvilla to his list of victims to finish with figures of six for 100 from 33 overs. Kuruvilla was out without scoring.
Nayan Mongia, who rescued India on Saturday, resumed at 74 but added only four before his attempted hook off captain and fast bowler Courtney Walsh was caught by Roland Holder at square leg.
Sunil Joshi, with a career-best 43 including three fours off 148 balls, frustrated the West Indian fast bowlers with a last-wicket partnership of 26 with Prasad before being bowled by Ian Bishop.
India had resumed at 308 for seven overnight.
